Container or bill of lading

How the check digit works

StepWhat happens
1Each letter becomes a number: A=10, B=12, C=13 … skipping every multiple of 11.
2Each of the first ten characters is multiplied by 2 raised to its position (1, 2, 4, 8 …).
3The total is divided by 11; the remainder is the check digit (10 is written as 0).

This is the ISO 6346 standard used on every marine container in the world. Rockit's team can trace a shipment for you at any point: call +20 2 2690 7601 or email support@rockit.com.eg.

A container number is four letters and seven digits. The last digit is a check digit calculated from the other ten characters, so a mistyped number is caught here before you go looking for it. Milestones are held by the shipping line, so once the number checks out we send you straight to that carrier's own tracking page.

Track with the carrier

If you already know the line, open its tracking page directly. Paste the number there.
